items.text: WTI and Brent crude have surged +10.3% and +7.6% respectively over the past week, driven by escalating Middle East tensions affecting supply expectations. Energy costs are becoming material to inflation narratives and corporate refinancing decisions; higher energy could slow credit fundamentals in sensitive sectors (transportation, petrochemicals, food production).

July payrolls plunged -23K (first decline since Oct 2025), unemployment held at 4.1%, and claims ticked up to 209K. Services employment also contracted sharply in July (ISM Services employment fell to 47.4). This signals early-cycle labor softening that could pressure household income and consumer credit quality, especially for lower-income cohorts already stressed by inflation.

July headline and core CPI both fell 0.1pp YoY to 3.4% and 2.5%, and core PCE is tracking near 3.3%. Energy is driving the variance; ex-energy, core inflation remains sticky. The flattening trajectory and Fed's pause mindset reduce near-term deflation tail risk but keep real rates challenged, supporting higher-for-longer duration risk for credit.

ECB deposit rate held at 2.25% as of mid-August, with markets pricing continued pause through end-Q3. US Fed funds flat at 3.75%. Curve steepened to 52bp (+4bp w/w) as 10Y rose to 4.72% and 2Y eased to 4.19%. Curve inversion is unwinding; neutral-to-accommodative policy backdrop supports credit valuations but duration volatility remains real given persistent inflation surprises.

HY OAS at 270bp (flat w/w) and IG OAS at 81bp (tight), while CCC OAS at 1018bp (-2bp) suggest binary credit dynamics: large-cap and high-quality benefiting from rate stability, but speculative/distressed cohorts remain vulnerable to credit events and refinancing stress. Spreads lack cushion for downside macro shocks.

Consumer sentiment plummeted to 51.0 in Aug from 55.2 in July, with both conditions and expectations declining sharply, and business condition expectations falling 11% short-term and 17% longer-term. Retail sales fell 0.6% in July, first decline since Oct 2025, signaling consumer pullback. Housing starts declined 12% YoY to 1.24M; weakness here threatens construction credit and developer refinancing windows.

GDPNow nowcast at 4.03% (vs 1.5% Q2 actual) reflects tentative optimism, but incoming July data show cracks: consumption cooling, labor deteriorating, confidence collapsing. Manufacturing PMI at 55.6 (strong) but China's official mfg PMI fell to 49.2, signaling global demand headwinds. Consensus is late-cycle deceleration into Q4; credit investors should expect widening volatility and selective default clusters.

themeCards.title: Labor Market Deterioration
themeCards.statusLine: July payrolls collapsed -23K (largest since 2024), unemployment holding at 4.1%, claims rising. Services employment contracted sharply (ISM emp index 47.4). Earliest tangible labor-market rollover on record in 2026.
themeCards.relevance: Threatens consumer credit fundamentals for subprime/prime auto, credit card, student loans. Wage growth stalling while inflation expectations sticky raises default risk; also signals recession probability rising, pressuring credit spreads across IG and HY.

themeCards.title: Consumer Confidence Cliff
themeCards.statusLine: Consumer sentiment fell sharply to 51.0 in early August from 55.2 in July, with deterioration broad-based across demographics, especially lower-income and less-educated cohorts. Earnings expectations and business-condition outlook collapsing.
themeCards.relevance: Critical signal for retail, discretionary, and consumer staple credit. Lower-income cohorts are credit-sensitive; deteriorating expectations predict near-term weakness in consumption-driven growth and near-term default risk in subprime pools and consumer-levered corporate credits.

themeCards.title: Energy Shock & Supply Chain Risk
themeCards.statusLine: WTI +10.3% to $84.77, Brent +7.6% to $93.26 over past week amid Middle East escalation. Geopolitical premium embedded in curves. Energy volatility now front-and-center risk factor.
themeCards.relevance: Immediate stress to energy-intensive corporate credits (logistics, chemicals, aviation, food production). Refinancing risk for levered energy producers if supply disruptions persist. Inflation re-acceleration tail risk pressures duration and rate expectations, widening credit spreads.

themeCards.title: Retail & Consumer Spending Rollover
themeCards.statusLine: Retail sales fell 0.6% m/m in July, first decline since Oct 2025, driven by weaker nonstore retail (-2.2%) and autos (-1.8%). Consumer pullback reflects both macro uncertainty and Amazon Prime Day timing shift.
themeCards.relevance: Threatens retail debt quality and consumer-discretionary credit. Combines with weak sentiment to signal demand weakness entering H2 2026; retail refinancing stress likely if spending momentum doesn't return; weakness in auto credit particularly acute given seasonal patterns.

themeCards.title: China Growth Stalling
themeCards.statusLine: China's manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2% in July, a 1.1pp drop, indicating declining manufacturing climate with production, new orders, and employment all below threshold. Signals demand shock from world's second-largest economy.
themeCards.relevance: Threatens credit quality for US exporters, multinational corporates, and commodity-linked credits (energy, metals, ag). Supply-chain gating risk if China demand continues to soften; refinancing pressure for companies with high Asia revenue exposure. Potential spillover to global growth assumptions underpinning credit ratings.

themeCards.title: Rate Volatility & Curve Repricing
themeCards.statusLine: 10Y UST rallied to 4.72%, 2Y eased to 4.19%, curve steepened to 52bp (from 48bp w/w). Energy shock and geopolitical premium creating short-term duration volatility; inflation expectations ticking up (1yr forecast now 4.3% per UMich).
themeCards.relevance: Credit investors face dual pressure: rising nominal rates challenge refinancing for floating-rate debt and extend duration for fixed-rate credits; curve dynamics signal investors repricing growth and inflation tail risks. Indebted credits with near-term maturities face higher rollover costs.

regime.label: Mid-Cycle Inflection
regime.detail: labor cracking, consumption cooling, confidence collapsing—growth deceleration with energy/geopolitical premium keeping inflation sticky, spreads tight and vulnerable to volatility
